resolutions.researcher_notes: Replaces dead petro-news.com/125650. Egypt Oil & Gas 'The Western Desert: Egypt's Giant Petroleum Reservoir' report (2020, FY2018/19 data). url_verifier returns 200 but cannot read PDF binary for the token; confirmed via pdftotext — the 'Natural Gas Infrastructure in the Western Desert' table lists BED/AS-Ameryia as one of the 13 existing/operating Western Desert gas pipelines, and the prose treats the southern-field-to-Mediterranean network as in-service. Supports Status=operating (single strong trade source; existence, not an explicit status word).

EOG Western Desert report gas-pipeline table (pdftotext): row 'BED/AS-Ameryia | BED/Abu Sennan connector | Ameryia | Length 160 | Diameter 24 | Capacity 350'. Capacity column header is (mmcf/d). Exactly supports Capacity=350.00 MMcf/d. Single authoritative trade source; no independent second source found for this obscure GPC intra-Western-Desert trunk line.

Same EOG Western Desert gas-pipeline table row (pdftotext): BED/AS-Ameryia Length (Km) = 160, Diameter 24 in. Exactly supports LengthKnown=160 km. Note a separate independent source (Future Pipe Industries) describes a DIFFERENT, shorter 24 km GRE gathering line inside the Abu Senan gas plant — not this 160 km BED/AS–Ameryia trunk; do not conflate the two.

FuelSource value is itself this EOG Western Desert report URL. The report documents the Western Desert gas fields (Abu Sennan/Abu Gharadig/Badr el Din southern fields) whose production feeds the Abu Sennan–Ameryia gas system; GPC's Abu Sennan gas/condensate plant (~85 mmcf/d) links southern-field production to the Mediterranean coast. Supports the fuel source. Same origin as the value; self-corroborating.

EOG Western Desert gas-pipeline table row (pdftotext): From = 'BED/Abu Sennan connector', To = 'Ameryia'. Supports StartLocation=Abu Sennan (Western Desert, Egypt) and End=Ameryia (Alexandria governorate, Egypt); Ameryia/Amreya is the Merghem/west-of-Alexandria LPG/gas plant per corroborating GASCO material. Table gives endpoints, not lat/long.

Two independent sources attribute the Abu Sennan gas-pipeline system to General Petroleum Company (GPC): (1) EOG Western Desert report — 'General Petroleum Company (GPC) established a plant for gas and condensate processing in Abu Sennan... the southern fields' production is linked to a distribution center on the Mediterranean Coast through Abu Sennan field'; (2) Future Pipe Industries — 'The General Petroleum Company (GPC) successfully operates its first phase of a Gas Pipeline in the Abu Senan area... Western Desert.' Supports Owner1=General Petroleum Co, 100%. The exact 100% share is not stated numerically (inferred single state operator); the two sources corroborate GPC as operator/owner, not the precise percentage.
